title: Web dev by day, first-time game dev by night: I made a card game with Claude and Gemini
author: montabone
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I'm a developer, and I make websites for a living. But I've always wanted to make games, and about a year ago I decided to stop just talking about it. My first attempt was a small quiz game a few months back. Asedra is my second, and the first one I feel proud enough to share here.

It's a card game where you play poker-style hands to knock down castle walls. If you've played Balatro you'll get it right away: you build combos, find relics that bend the rules, and try to get through every siege. It's set in the Middle Ages and looks like an old illuminated manuscript, with a little monk narrating the story (and crossing out the parts he'd rather you didn't read).

About the AI part: the art is all Gemini. I wrote the prompts, kept what looked good and fixed a lot of things by hand. Claude helped me a lot with the code and with testing the balance. I come from web dev, not games, so having something to bounce ideas off was a big help.

It wasn't as easy as I thought, though. The AI gives you a first draft super fast, but making everything look like it belongs to the same world took me forever. Balancing was the same: numbers that looked fine on paper felt terrible when I actually played.

It's been out for about a week and only like 15 people have installed it so far, so yeah, very small for now.

It's free, with no purchases. The only ads are optional ones you can watch for a few extra moves. It's in Spanish and English, Android only for now.  
  
[Asedra: Roguelike de Cartas - Aplicaciones en Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.secretlabs.asedio)

  
I'd really like to hear what you think, especially if something is confusing or too easy. And if you're also a "regular dev trying to make games" like me, I'd love to hear how you're doing it. Happy to answer anything about how I used AI!

P.S. I'm from Chile and my English isn't 100% perfect, so sorry in advance if something sounds weird or is written wrong, haha. Feel free to correct me!
